claim.why_it_matters: A heading nested at the wrong level breaks the section tree a clause lookup walks: 6.11.4 reads as a sibling of 6.11 instead of its child.
claim.note: Heading at the wrong level: same as p313-1; parent '### 6.11' and siblings '#### 6.11.1', '#### 6.11.2' on page 312, so 6.11.4 should be '####'.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page VI-81 shows the heading '6.11.4 General Rules', a subclause of 6.11 by its numbering. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md, line 12931 is '### 6.11 THE DIVIDE STATEMENT', lines 12933 and 12937 are '#### 6.11.1 Function' and '#### 6.11.2 General Format', but line 13028 is '### 6.11.4 General Rules'. That is the same level as its parent, so the markdown section tree makes 6.11.4 a sibling of 6.11. The words are the same in both sources. The defect is the heading level, not a missing heading. The neighbouring clauses are each consistent within themselves: 6.10 uses ##/### and 6.12 uses ####. The fix is '#### 6.11.4 General Rules'.
verdict.corrected_description: Heading level is wrong; the heading is not missing. The markdown has '### 6.11.4 General Rules' under '### 6.11 THE DIVIDE STATEMENT', whose other children 6.11.1 and 6.11.2 are '####'. It should be '#### 6.11.4 General Rules' (kind: wrong-heading-level).
